Question
========
Consider a server with one service station and infinite buffer capacity. It receives a request every 50 milliseconds on average according to a Poisson distribution. The observed service times in ms are:

23, 21, 20, 21, 24, 22, 21, 24, 24, 20, 20, 22, 21, 23, 24

(a) What is the expected response time of the system?
(b) What is the expected queue length?

Solution
========
Arrivals are Poisson, service times are measured and not exponential, so this is M/G/1.

The 15 samples sum to 330, so E[S] = 22 ms. Their squares sum to 7294, so E[S2] = 486.3 ms2.

lambda = 1/50 = 0.02 per ms, so rho = lambda x E[S] = 22/50 = 0.44.

E[W] = lambda x E[S2] / (2 (1 - rho)) = (0.02 x 486.3) / (2 x 0.56) = 9.73 / 1.12 = 8.7 ms.

(a) E[R] = E[W] + E[S] = 8.7 + 22 = 30.7 ms.

(b) The queue length is the number waiting, so by Little's law applied to the queue, E[Nw] = lambda x E[W] = 0.02 x 8.7 = 0.17 job.

Careful not to answer E[N], which also counts the job in service and would be 0.17 + 0.44 = 0.61.
